title: The 3 Best Resistance Bands for Physical Therapy
h1: The 3 Best Resistance Bands for Physical Therapy
metaDescription: Our 3 picks for resistance bands for physical therapy, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at resistance bands for physical therapy using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: TheraBand Resistance Bands Set, Beginner Kit
products.blurb: Key specs: 3 flat bands: yellow, red, green, 3.0 to 6.7 lbs progressive resistance, Non-latex option available.
strengths: The exact brand and color system most home exercise handouts from clinics reference
Gentle starting resistance appropriate for post-surgical or early-stage rehab
Flat shape anchors easily around a door, chair leg, or limb
Non-latex version avoids a common allergy concern in clinical settings
limitations: No handles included, so grip fatigue can show up before the muscle does on longer sets
Tops out at 6.7 lbs, which some rehab protocols outgrow after several weeks
5-foot length needs to be folded or shortened for many single-limb exercises
features: Used in outpatient PT clinics nationally

products.name: BalanceFrom Resistance Loop Exercise Bands, Set of 7
products.blurb: Key specs: 7 loop bands, XX-light to XX-heavy, 12-inch by 2-inch natural latex loops, Carrying bag and exercise card included.
strengths: Closed loop shape is the correct tool for clamshells, lateral walks, and hip abduction rehab
XX-light band is gentle enough for early post-op hip and knee protocols
Seven levels give a long runway before needing a second set
Low cost makes it easy for a clinic to recommend without price pushback
limitations: Less useful than flat bands for upper-body or shoulder rehab anchoring
No handles, so grip-dependent exercises are limited
Loops can roll on the thigh during longer clamshell sets
features: Carrying bag and exercise card included

products.name: Bodylastics Resistance Bands Basic Tension Edition
products.blurb: Key specs: 4 continuous tube bands, stackable, Padded handles and ankle straps included, Carabiner clip system, up to 44 lbs per side.
strengths: Stackable resistance lets a patient progress from light rehab load to real strength work on one set
Ankle straps support later-stage leg rehab exercises that loops and flat bands cannot anchor as securely
Anti-snap inner cord is a meaningful safety margin for a home-use rehab tool
Handles reduce grip fatigue during higher-rep rehab sets
limitations: Higher resistance floor than TheraBand, not ideal for the earliest post-injury stage
More setup than a flat band or loop, an issue for patients with limited hand dexterity
Not the brand most home exercise handouts specifically reference
features: Padded handles and ankle straps included
Carabiner clip system, up to 44 lbs per side
Included user book and workout DVD

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
